type: var1.machine-guide.v1
product: VANTARI-ONE
runtime: apps/backend
contract: AGENTS.md
architecture: apps/backend/architecture.md
current_summary: .docs/technical_summary.md
workspace_record: .docs/workspace.json
execution_roadmap: .docs/roadmap/24-harness-capability-next-90.md

VANTARI is a local Zig agent kernel. Prompts control voice, pace, initiative,
delegation, and interaction cadence. The kernel controls executable capability,
durability, budgets, evidence, recovery, and irreversible-action gates.

TUI Shift+Tab cycles the session-local prompt mode `orchestrate`, `build`,
`align`, `plan`; the next `session/send` carries the exact label, omission
defaults to `orchestrate`, and unknown labels fail before execution. Prompt mode
changes provider guidance only; it does not change the executor, tools, access,
model, or capacity.

The assembled provider-facing system prompt is bounded by
`context.prompt_budget_tokens` (default `8192`) through the existing context
policy. The builder returns `PromptBudgetExceeded` before provider dispatch
instead of truncating prompt layers. Native provider tool schemas remain a
separate API surface inside the full context-window budget. Behavior profiles
are prompt-owned and source-tested across all four modes and root/recon/
orchestrator tool routes without executor branches. `TokenPrecision` carries
exact provider usage, estimated compiler context, or unknown accounting through
the existing turn events; exactness is never inferred from `chars / 4`.

The context compiler is the sole provider-window builder. It preserves the
append-only transcript, reports synthesized interrupted tool results and
skipped orphan/mismatched rows through `var1.context_compile_diagnostic.v1`,
and provider-overflow recovery rebuilds from the checkpoint plus durable
suffix before one retry. The TUI suppresses this mechanics event in silent and
normal posture; full logs show compact counts.

The TUI footer is one non-wrapping read model: status, prompt mode, model,
effort, context used/capacity/percent, and remaining context. Active/max agents
and queue pressure are signal-gated; finite priced session cost may share the
lower-signal segment only for exact telemetry. Estimated context carries `~`;
unknown used/remaining context is `ctx — / capacity`. `/status` suppresses
partial cumulative totals. No footer registry, cost poller, progress gauge,
second row, or status bus exists.

Agent activity uses the same keyed parent-event projection and child
`sessions/summaries.jsonl` boundary: groups show `Agents completed/total`, `○`
means queued/running, `◉` means complete, and each child keeps a bounded quoted
summary. The existing `update_session_summary` completion refreshes that quote
while the child is running; later tool/terminal phases retain it. Known typed phase and elapsed
snapshots use the same row and yield to the summary when width is tight.
`tool_completed` is typed event metadata, not the visible child conclusion; there
is no bubble event, poller, or second summary ledger.

Canonical execution path:
operator input -> public LocalClient facade -> project-local execution owner ->
private ChildClient -> kernel-stdio -> transcript/context/provider/tools/events ->
durable terminal state.

Canonical runtime state:
.var/sessions/<session-id>/session.json
.var/sessions/<session-id>/messages.jsonl
.var/sessions/<session-id>/context.jsonl
.var/sessions/<session-id>/events.jsonl
.var/sessions/<session-id>/output.txt

Owner state:
.var/runtime/execution-owner.json
apps/backend/src/host/owner_client.zig
apps/backend/src/host/owner_state.zig
apps/backend/src/host/http_bridge.zig
apps/backend/src/host/stdio_client.zig
apps/backend/src/core/agents/spec.zig
apps/backend/src/core/agents/service.zig
apps/backend/src/core/agents/mailbox.zig

Rules:
- Clients render kernel-owned state and never assemble provider context.
- One workspace has one owner, one private kernel child, one agent pool, and one
  scheduler composition.
- Client exit does not stop the owner. Foreground serve and automatic owner start
  share one lease.
- Tickets own work lifecycle. Assignment is queue admission, not execution.
- Tickets are the only work-lifecycle owner; summaries are bounded handoff
  projections and plans/research/advice/roadmap/changelog are ticket-linked
  artifacts. The runtime does not create or read `todo_slice`, `session_record`,
  `.var/todos/`, or per-session `session.md` records.
- agent_routes.max_concurrency is the sole ticket execution capacity setting;
  running is active, idle=max-running, queued is admitted backlog, and
  available=idle-queued saturated at zero. A changed value replaces the same
  pool at its next idle boundary; there is no tickets execution-policy branch.
- messages.jsonl remains complete and append-only; every row has a durable
  generated or explicit deterministic ID. context.jsonl is a model-visible
  checkpoint ledger, not a transcript, and records inclusive source ranges plus
  first_kept_seq for cold replay.
- Use typed tools and advertised availability. search_files requires ix.
- Session-owned file mutations reserve a provider tool-call intent before
  `write_file`/`append_file`/`replace_in_file`, commit measured effect evidence
  after mutation, and close unresolved reservations as `abandoned` at safe cold
  start. No rollback is claimed without byte evidence.
- runtime.full_access_mode is false by default; resolved child routes carry it
  into the shared file/search/LSP/shell execution context, and it never relocates
  .var.
- Auth uses one provider ledger: installed `$VANTARI_HOME/auth.json` or
  workspace `.var/auth.json`; `auth status --json` is secret-free, `auth login
  openai-codex` owns PKCE persistence, and `auth logout <provider-id>` removes
  one record. OAuth `openai-codex` routes through `core/providers/openai_codex.zig`
  to `/codex/responses` with account/originator metadata; API-key providers keep
  the OpenAI-compatible route and never fall back across the auth boundary.
- Provider-scoped API-key login supports Anthropic Messages, OpenRouter and
  explicit custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Use `auth login <id>` with
  `--api-key-stdin` or `--api-key-env`, `auth use <id>` for active selection,
  `providers --json` for secret-free inventory, `models --provider <id>` for
  discovery, and `run --provider <id> --model <id>` or
  `session/send.provider_id` for per-turn routing. Custom records explicitly
  choose base URL, wire API, and bearer/API-key/no-auth header scheme.
- Scheduler leadership is process-exclusive and generation-fenced in source.
- Ticket claim, worker generation, lease, capability, and deterministic child
  identity commit in one process-serialized ticket row before child creation.
- Expired claims settle terminal evidence first. Existing nonterminal sessions
  resume through one generation-fenced ticket row with the same attempt, receipt,
  transcript, and mailbox cursor; only absent sessions requeue. Heartbeat requires
  exact live Supervisor ownership.
- agents {} returns var1.agent_eligibility.v1: sorted route-resolvable
  specialists, unavailable route classes, fixed-pool/team pressure,
  communication choices, and a SHA-256 receipt. Prompts choose solo, inspect,
  message, challenge, launch, queue, or wake; launch/config revalidates effects.
- Agent messaging uses one events.jsonl mailbox: direct, parent, current_group;
  queue/wake; durable recipient sequence, sender receipt, and provider-success
  unread cursor. Messages never assign tickets, launch work, or copy transcripts.
- Root interaction uses one `ask_user` tool and one `input/respond` RPC. The tool
  emits bounded `var1.input_requested.v1` event data, the TUI renders a
  settings-style horizontal-row panel with clamped question/option focus,
  Enter select, Space check, `f / Other` inline text, and an explicit review
  state. Display text is frame-sanitized, static option keys preserve original
  response ids, and clipped viewports are guarded. Malformed requests become one bounded message plus run cancellation;
  terminal/error boundaries clear stale panel state, active Ctrl-C uses the same
  input cancellation route, and the session cancel/shutdown path wakes the same broker wait. Child profiles omit the tool and fail closed
  with `InputUnavailable`; do not add a question poller or second status bus.
- Root normal, root-agent, and orchestrator-only catalogs retain `ask_user`,
  while the orchestrator allow-list continues to deny artifact and command
  tools. `orchestrate`, `build`, `align`, and `plan` share the same Vaxis-tested
  question controller.
- TTSR matches stop provider reads through one typed stream abort hook before
  terminal completion. The executor persists correction plus `rule_injected`
  evidence and retries through the existing loop; installed provider proof is
  still deferred.
- The source and installed Windows lifecycle meshes prove queue-only assignment,
  one claim, client detach, exact owner-tree loss, generation replacement,
  same-session resume, nested direct/group/parent delivery, one terminal ticket,
  cold readback, and zero proof-owned processes. Do not infer exactly-once
  arbitrary external effects; that remains a separate roadmap gate.

Commands from apps/backend:
scripts/zigw.ps1 build test --summary all
zig-out/bin/vantari.exe health --json
zig-out/bin/vantari.exe run --prompt "..."
scripts/prove-ticket-lifecycle.ps1 -BinaryPath zig-out/bin/vantari.exe
zig-out/bin/vantari.exe serve --port 4310
scripts/prove-owner-tracer.ps1 -BinaryPath zig-out/bin/vantari.exe -EntryPoint serve
scripts/prove-owner-lifecycle.ps1 -BinaryPath zig-out/bin/vantari.exe -ConcurrentClients 20
